subject: Latency-first: TTFT targets and streaming cadence recap
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finflow.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finflow.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency/streaming recap

Karthik / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — this is a quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on what we need and to confirm next steps. I’ve attached a rough performance matrix that maps our expected traffic patterns. High level: 

- Primary goal: minimize time-to-first-token (TTFT) for interactive flows (customer chat UI). Target: 150–250 ms median; 95th under 400 ms for typical 256-token prompts.
- Streaming: we will use WebSocket in the browser for desktop, but need an SSE fallback for mobile clients (iOS background limitations).
- Chunk cadence: prefer smaller frequent chunks to improve perceived responsiveness. Goal: chunks every 150–300 ms or ~40–150 tokens per chunk depending on model output pacing.
- Throughput: baseline 40 requests/sec, expected sustained 100k tokens/day; burst to 200 req/sec during peak campaigns.
- Concurrency per user: up to 3 concurrent streams; global concurrency for the app expected ~600 parallel streams during peak.

Open questions we want help on: model selection (latency-optimized variants), whether prefix caching / KV-cache will help TTFT for our traffic, recommended batching settings that preserve our latency targets, and fallback strategy when WebSocket saturates.

Next steps from our side: attach attendee list and performance matrix. Would like a concrete pilot/runbook and a short performance probe we can run (48–72 hours) to validate 95th percentile TTFT and streaming chunk cadence.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | FinFlow
attach: FinFlow_performance_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 17:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency/streaming recap

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the matrix, that’s really helpful. Quick confirmation and a proposed path forward: 

1) Restating target: TTFT median 150–250 ms, p95 < 400 ms (256-token prompts) — we can run probes to validate across regions.
2) Streaming approach: WebSocket primary + SSE fallback for mobile — we recommend starting with WebSocket and a 200 ms chunk cadence target (tunable). We’ll instrument perceived latency metrics (TTFT + first-chunk time).
3) Model/serving options: two suggested variants — a latency-optimized quantized model (fast single-GPU TTFT) and a standard model for quality. We’ll surface cost/latency tradeoffs in the pilot.
4) Caching: prefix/KV caching should help for templated prompts; we’ll quantify expected TTFT improvements given your prompt distribution.
5) Throughput & concurrency: pilot config proposal below.

Proposed pilot (48–72 hours):
- Environment: Dedicated test pool that mirrors your prod region (us-west).
- Load: synthetic mix that mirrors your matrix: ~40 sustained req/s with engineered bursts to 200 req/s for 10–20 minute windows.
- Metrics: median TTFT, p95 TTFT, first-chunk time, chunk size distribution, tokens/sec, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Acceptance: p95 TTFT < 400 ms for >= 95% of test window and first-chunk time < 250 ms for interactive users.

Attachments: I’m attaching a draft SLA/proposal and will upload a short runbook for the probe. Can you confirm whether FinFlow can run a short synthetic probe from a staging region (we can provide a probe script), or would you prefer Redwood run the probe and share logs?

Next steps / action items:
- Alex: confirm you want Redwood to orchestrate the probe or provide scripts (reply here).
- Ben: can you scope a pilot pack (env + probes + dashboard)?
- I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min pilot kickoff.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finflow.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency/streaming recap

Alex — quick note from me: we’ll package a pilot that includes: dedicated test pool (2x small GPU nodes), a Redis-backed KV cache option for templated prompts, and an observability dashboard with TTFT and chunk cadence graphs.

I’ll also add a short doc with recommended WebSocket keepalive and chunk-size heuristics (we’ve found 100–200 token chunks with a 150–250 ms cadence gives the best perceived responsiveness for similar apps).

Tentative timing: can start pilot as early as next week (12/14) if you approve. I’ll prepare the DocuSign for a short pilot agreement and the SLA-proposal draft Karthik mentioned.

Thanks — cc’ing Karthik to set the kickoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
attach: SLA-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finflow.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finflow.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency/streaming recap

Ben / Karthik — this looks good. We want Redwood to run the probe and share the logs/dashboards; please include our mobile product lead (Sonia, cc’d) in the kickoff.

Approved tentative start: 2026-12-14. Please send the pilot agreement and a calendar invite for the kickoff. Sonia — quick note on mobile: we’ll validate SSE fallback in a small set of internal devices during the pilot; expect an additional test case around background iOS behavior.

Thanks,
Alex
